label: Life
scope_note: Living things and their processes: cells, genes and organisms, their diversity, evolution and ecology.

label: Cell biology
scope_note: The structure and function of cells, the basic units of life.

label: Molecular biology
scope_note: How DNA, RNA and proteins carry, express and regulate genetic information.

label: Genetics
scope_note: Genes, heredity and variation in living things.

label: Genomics
scope_note: Whole genomes: their sequencing, structure, function and comparison.

label: Evolution
scope_note: Descent with modification: how populations change over generations through natural selection and other processes.

label: Speciation
scope_note: How new species arise.

label: Phylogenetics and systematics
scope_note: Reconstructing the evolutionary relationships among organisms: the tree of life.

label: Origin of life
scope_note: How life first arose from non-living chemistry.

label: Human evolution
scope_note: The evolutionary history of humans and their closest extinct relatives.

label: Physiology
scope_note: How living organisms and their parts function.

label: Developmental biology
scope_note: How organisms grow and develop from a single cell.

label: Ecology
scope_note: The relationships of organisms with each other and with their environment.

label: Ecosystems
scope_note: Communities of organisms together with their physical environment, and the flows of energy and matter through them.

label: Biomes
scope_note: Major kinds of ecosystem shaped by climate: forests, grasslands, deserts, tundra, wetlands, reefs and others.

label: Biogeography
scope_note: Why living things are distributed where they are, across space and through time.

label: Biodiversity and conservation
scope_note: The variety of life, the threats to it, and efforts to protect species and ecosystems.

label: Diversity of life
scope_note: The kinds of living things (and viruses) and how they are classified.

label: Biological classification
scope_note: Naming and classifying organisms, from Linnaean ranks to modern phylogenetic classifications and folk taxonomies.

label: Microorganisms
scope_note: Microscopic life and its study: bacteria, archaea, protists, microscopic fungi, and viruses.

label: Bacteria and archaea
scope_note: Single-celled organisms without a nucleus, the oldest and most numerous forms of life.

label: Viruses
scope_note: Infectious agents that replicate only inside living cells; whether they count as alive is debated.

label: Protists
scope_note: Mostly single-celled organisms with a nucleus that are not plants, animals or fungi.

label: Fungi
scope_note: Mushrooms, moulds and yeasts, and their study.

label: Plants
scope_note: Plants and their study, from mosses to flowering trees.

label: Animals
scope_note: Animals and their study.

label: Invertebrates
scope_note: Animals without a backbone — insects, molluscs, worms, crustaceans and many more — the vast majority of animal species.

label: Fish
scope_note: Aquatic vertebrates with gills: jawless, cartilaginous and bony fishes.

label: Amphibians
scope_note: Frogs, salamanders and caecilians.

label: Reptiles
scope_note: Turtles, lizards, snakes, crocodilians and their relatives.

label: Birds
scope_note: Birds and their study.

label: Mammals
scope_note: Mammals, including humans' closest relatives.

label: Animal behaviour
scope_note: The behaviour of animals and its evolution.

label: Marine biology
scope_note: Life in the seas and oceans.
